content:
iPhone Bumper cases have been popular with users ever since the iPhone 4 bumper, but in recent years the available options have dwindled. Rhinoshield offers a solid choice for users who prefer a minimalist style.

Last year Apple finally returned to the bumper case market with the iPhone Air. I had been hoping Apple would extend its bumper case to the iPhone 18 Pro (just as it had previously expanded its clear case to the iPhone 11), but unfortunately that never happened. While searching for alternatives, I came across Rhinoshield's Minimalist Impact Bumper case.

Key Details

The fit of the Impact Bumper is similar to that of most other bumper cases — the lip around the screen is fairly subtle, while the lip on the back is slightly more pronounced. The case has a unique design feature that I particularly appreciate: a special support structure that prevents the camera plateau and lenses from making direct contact with the surface the phone is placed on. With the aluminium bodies of the 17 Pro and 18 Pro, I especially value this feature. This design gives the case far greater protective capability than a typical bumper, while also solving the annoying rocking issue when using the phone on a flat surface.

The fit, however, leaves something to be desired. Once installed, the case is slightly loose, and the edges are easy to peel outward — I am also concerned that prolonged use may cause warping. While I don't think the phone will fly out of the case when dropped (and I have inadvertently tested this), the entire case is made of hard plastic rather than rubber, so I hope it holds up over the long term. Rhinoshield says the case is made from a single material, making it 100% recyclable.

The case is offered in three colours that complement the iPhone 18 Pro finishes: white, blue and black (fans of the Deep Purple colourway will be disappointed). I chose the blue, which is close to but not quite identical to the Glacier finish.

Downsides

It isn't without its downsides, though. My main complaint about this case is that the buttons are difficult to press. This is probably due to the near-flush design combined with the button construction — the feel is soft and lacks tactile definition.

The overall material choice may also be a downside. For me, the texture of this case doesn't feel quite as refined as Apple's iPhone Air bumper, though some may actually prefer the feel. Compared with the materials used in typical TPU/rubber clear cases, I definitely prefer this one. However, the material and looser fit seem to attract all the dust from inside a bag.

If you use Apple's Wrist Strap or Crossbody Strap, note that this case has no attachment points for either.

Conclusion

The Rhinoshield bumper case is far from perfect, and I still hope Apple will extend its bumper case to other iPhone models. Ultimately, however, I decided to stick with this case, for one main reason: it offers a near-naked-phone experience without the worry of the aluminium body getting scratched or dented. This bumper case appears to be generally available only through Rhinoshield's own website, priced at around US$30 after shipping — comparable to Apple's US$39 case. You can buy the Rhinoshield Minimalist Impact Bumper case here. (Amazon listings do pop up from time to time, so you could also try buying it there.)
